title: Parliament protest-camp rallies, February 19–20
location: In front of the Parliament of Georgia, Tbilisi
scope: Local action; whether the February 19 and 20 gatherings form one continuous episode remains unresolved.
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. HRC and Civil Georgia report about 20 initial detentions and five additional activists detained at a later rally; arrests are not total attendance, and neither reviewed passage gives a crowd count or establishes >=50 attendees.

title.summary: HRC describes Parliament rallies on February 19–20 and attempts to erect protest camps; Civil Georgia reports the February 19 tent confrontation.

start_date.summary: The HRC report dates the Parliament rallies to February 19–20, 2021; February 19 is used as the earliest reported day.

location.summary: HRC places the rallies in front of the Parliament of Georgia in Tbilisi.

organizer.summary: Not identified in the reviewed passages.

demands.summary: The reviewed HRC and Civil Georgia passages do not establish an exact participant-attributed demand; no category assigned.

participants.summary: Reports of 20 initial detentions and five additional arrests are response counts; no total attendance or >=50 threshold evidence is provided.

end_date.summary: The reviewed passages cover February 19–20 activity but do not establish the physical end or whether the gatherings were continuous.

state_response.summary: HRC reports police prevented tent erection and about 20 activists were arrested; Civil Georgia reports five further detentions and quotes the Public Defender criticizing the tent seizure. Other response values remain unknown.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown; Civil Georgia’s description of a “physical confrontation” does not attribute violence to participants.

notes: Research candidate only. HRC and Civil Georgia establish Parliament-area protest activity and arrests, but not total attendance, an exact participant demand, organizer, physical end, or whether February 19 and 20 were one continuous action. Detentions are not turnout. The body read concerns the February 19–20 tent episode; do not conflate it with the February 23 Nika Melia raid, the later opposition rallies, or the February 28 Kutaisi HPP rally.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people attend on either February 19 or February 20?
What demand and organizer did participants identify?
Were the February 19 and 20 gatherings one continuous action or separate events?
When did the physical gathering end?
Were there further event-specific state responses beyond the reported detentions and tent restriction?

title: Kutaisi rally against the Namakhvani HPP project (February 28)
location: Downtown Kutaisi; the planned rally near the ENKA office in Opurchkheti was moved to Kutaisi.
scope: Local public rally against the Namakhvani HPP project; separate from the pre-existing Rioni Valley camp/shift rotation.
organizer: Varlam Goletiani, identified by Civil Georgia as a movement organizer; the exact formal organizing body is not established in the reviewed passage.
threshold_50_evidence: Civil Georgia describes thousands gathering downtown in Kutaisi; this qualitative report clearly exceeds the 50-person threshold, but does not provide an exact count.

title.summary: Civil Georgia reports a large rally in Kutaisi against the Namakhvani HPP project.

start_date.summary: The article dates the Kutaisi rally to February 28, 2021.

location.summary: The event took place downtown in Kutaisi after a plan to gather near the ENKA office in Opurchkheti was changed.

organizer.summary: Varlam Goletiani is identified as a movement organizer and is quoted at the rally; the precise legal/formal organizer name remains uncertain.

demands.summary: The article reports calls for the Georgian Government to revoke the project permission and for ENKA to leave the Rioni Gorge; it also describes demands to cancel ownership and construction orders. Coded as a land/resource issue.

participants.summary: Civil Georgia says “thousands”; exact attendance and numerical range are not provided.

end_date.summary: The reviewed passage does not establish the gathering’s physical end.

state_response.summary: No event-specific state response is established by the reviewed article passage.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown; the reviewed article passage does not assess protester violence.

notes: Candidate only; not human-approved or an official MM event. The source’s qualitative “thousands” supports the threshold without an exact count. Do not carry the separate camp’s crowd count into this rally or treat the February 28 Kutaisi gathering as a continuation with the camp. Civil Georgia separately reports that the camp maintained rotating shifts for over 100 days; exact start/end remain unknown.
open_questions: When did the physical rally end?
Can another independent contemporary source verify the qualitative crowd estimate and stated demands?
Were there event-specific state actions beyond those covered by the reviewed article?
